sourceReview: Read bundled BSB Psalm 57 in full with each verse's related passages before drafting. References are thematic or literary comparisons, not an invented historical occasion. Scripture is never stored in the notes; it loads from the bundled BSB.

study.title: In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter.
study.intro: Eleven verses move from a cave where David hid from Saul, sheltering under God's wings among lions, to a steadfast heart that wakes the dawn with music and praises God among the nations.
study.context: The heading names David, the tune 'Do Not Destroy' (also on Psalms 58, 59 and 75), and the occasion 'when he fled from Saul into the cave.' That may be the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1) or the cave at En-gedi where David spared Saul's life (1 Samuel 24:1–7). A refrain, 'Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth,' closes both halves (verses 5 and 11). Verses 1–6 describe danger and trust; verses 7–11 burst into praise. Verses 7–11 are reused almost word for word in Psalm 108:1–5. 'Lions' in verse 4 are a picture of violent men whose words wound, not literal animals in the cave. The Scripture is loaded unchanged from the bundled BSB, including the heading.
study.peopleNote: The heading names David and the time he fled from Saul into the cave. His profile includes his years hiding from Saul in the wilderness caves of Adullam and En-gedi. Saul is named in the heading but has no profile. Planned paintings show caves, wings of birds, lions, a harp at dawn and wide skies; God is never portrayed as a human body.

verses.title: The shadow of Your wings
verses.heading: Refuge in a cave
verses.meaning: The heading names David, the tune 'Do Not Destroy,' and the occasion: David fled from Saul into a cave. He asks twice for mercy. His soul takes refuge in God. In the shadow of God's wings he will shelter until danger passes. A cave was physical shelter, but David's true refuge is God. The image of wings pictures a mother bird covering her young.
verses.context: Ruth 2:12 speaks of refuge under the LORD's wings, and Matthew 23:37 records Jesus longing to gather Jerusalem as a hen gathers her chicks. 1 Samuel 22:1 and 24:3 record David in caves.
explore: Have mercy, have mercy
The double plea shows urgency. David depends on God's grace.
Until the danger has passed
Shelter is for a time. David trusts the storm will end.
verses.reflect: What danger do you need to wait out under God's wings?
verses.alt: A mother bird shelters her chicks under spread wings in a rocky cleft.

verses.title: God who fulfills His purpose
verses.heading: Crying to the Most High
verses.meaning: I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me. David calls to God Most High, above every power, including Saul. He trusts that God will complete what He has planned for him. David had been anointed king (1 Samuel 16:13), but now he hides in a cave. He believes God will finish what He began. The verse is confident trust in God's purpose despite circumstances.
verses.context: Psalm 138:8 says, 'The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me,' and Philippians 1:6 says He who began a good work will complete it. 1 Samuel 16:13 records David's anointing.
explore: God Most High
God is above every power. Saul's threat is beneath Him.
Fulfills His purpose
God completes His plans. David trusts He will finish what He began.
verses.reflect: What purpose do you trust God to fulfill in your life despite present circumstances?
verses.alt: A horn of anointing oil rests on a ledge inside a dim cave.

verses.title: Loving devotion and truth
verses.heading: Rescue from heaven
verses.meaning: He reaches down from heaven and saves me; He rebukes those who trample me. Selah. God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth. David pictures God sending help from heaven, as though reaching down. God rebukes or shames those who trample him. Selah pauses mid-verse. Then God's loving devotion and truth are sent like two messengers. Covenant love and faithfulness are David's rescuers.
verses.context: Psalm 43:3 asks God to send out His light and truth, and Psalm 18:16 says, 'He reached down from on high and took hold of me.' Psalm 57:3 pictures love and truth sent to rescue.
explore: Reaches down from heaven
God sends help from heaven. Rescue comes from above, not from the cave's walls.
Loving devotion and truth
God's covenant love and faithfulness are sent. They protect David.
verses.reflect: How have you seen God's loving devotion and truth come to your aid?
verses.alt: Two beams of light descend through clouds into a ravine.

verses.title: Among the lions
verses.heading: Surrounded by violent men
verses.meaning: My soul is among the lions; I lie down with ravenous beasts, with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords. David describes his enemies as lions. They are men whose words are weapons. He must lie down among them, perhaps meaning he lives surrounded by danger. The image combines violence and speech. Their tongues wound like swords. Yet David has just affirmed God's rescue.
verses.context: Daniel 6:22 records God shutting the lions' mouths, and Psalm 55:21 describes words that are swords. Psalm 57:4 uses lions as a picture of violent men.
explore: Among the lions
David's enemies are fierce as lions. He has to live and sleep among danger.
Tongues are sharp swords
Their words wound like blades. Speech becomes a weapon against David.
verses.reflect: Where do you feel surrounded by danger? How does God's rescue change that?
verses.alt: Lions rest in a rocky wilderness at the edge of a cave.

verses.title: Be exalted above the heavens
verses.heading: The first refrain
verses.meaning: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth. In the middle of danger, David turns to worship. He asks God to be exalted, lifted up, above the heavens. He prays that God's glory would fill the earth. This is the first refrain; it returns in verse 11. David's concern shifts from his own safety to God's glory. Worship is his response to fear.
verses.context: Habakkuk 2:14 says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, and Isaiah 6:3 says the whole earth is full of His glory. Psalm 57:5 and 11 share this refrain.
explore: Be exalted
David wants God honored above all. His focus is on God.
Glory cover the earth
God's glory should fill the world. David prays for this.
verses.reflect: How could you shift your focus from your own trouble to God's glory today?
verses.alt: Sunrise light floods across a vast earth from a high peak.

verses.title: They fell into their own pit
verses.heading: The trap reversed
verses.meaning: They spread a net for my feet; my soul was despondent. They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it! Selah. David's enemies set traps, a net and a pit, as hunters do. His soul was bowed down. But the trap caught its makers. At En-gedi, Saul came into the very cave where David hid, and David spared him (1 Samuel 24:3–7). Selah marks the reversal.
verses.context: Psalm 7:15 says the one who digs a pit falls into it, and Proverbs 26:27 repeats the idea. 1 Samuel 24:3–7 records Saul entering David's cave and David sparing him.
explore: Spread a net
Enemies set traps like hunters. Every step David took was in danger.
Fallen into it
The trap caught its own makers. The evil they planned recoiled on them.
verses.reflect: Have you seen evil plans backfire? How does that encourage trust in God?
verses.alt: A hunter's net hangs tangled and empty over a dug pit.

verses.title: My heart is steadfast
verses.heading: A firm and ready heart
verses.meaning: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music. The tone shifts to confident praise. David's heart is firm, fixed and ready. The repetition shows conviction. Despite danger, he is settled. He will sing and make music. This line begins the section reused in Psalm 108:1. Faith becomes song.
verses.context: Psalm 108:1 repeats this verse, and Psalm 112:7 says the righteous will not fear bad news because their heart is steadfast. Psalm 57:7 sings from a settled heart.
explore: Steadfast
David's heart is firm and ready. It is not shaken by the danger outside the cave.
Sing and make music
Praise flows from a steady heart. Music expresses trust.
verses.reflect: What would help make your heart steadfast in God today?
verses.alt: A harp leans steady against a rock at the mouth of a cave.

verses.title: I will awaken the dawn
verses.heading: Music before sunrise
verses.meaning: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn. David calls his own soul, his 'glory,' to wake up. He calls his instruments to wake. Then he says he will wake the dawn itself. Instead of waiting for morning to wake him, he will rise before it and greet it with music. The verse is bold and joyful.
verses.context: Psalm 108:2 repeats this verse, and Mark 1:35 records Jesus rising very early to pray. Lamentations 3:22–23 says God's mercies are new every morning.
explore: Awake, my glory
David rouses his inner self. He calls his soul to worship.
Awaken the dawn
David rises before sunrise. His praise greets the morning.
verses.reflect: What would it look like to greet tomorrow's dawn with praise?
verses.alt: A lyre rests on a hilltop rock as the first sunrise glow spreads.

verses.title: Among the nations
verses.heading: Praise for all peoples
verses.meaning: I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples. David's praise is not just for Israel. He will praise God among the nations. A fugitive in a cave vows to sing to the world. This anticipates God's purpose to bless all nations. Paul quotes a similar line in Romans 15:9 to show the gospel's reach to Gentiles.
verses.context: Romans 15:9 quotes Psalm 18:49, 'I will praise You among the Gentiles,' and Psalm 96:3 says, 'Declare His glory among the nations.' Psalm 57:9 has the same vision.
explore: Among the nations
David's praise is for the world. It is not limited to Israel.
Among the peoples
God's praise is meant for everyone. David will sing it widely.
verses.reflect: How could your praise of God reach beyond your own circle?
verses.alt: A caravan crossroads market hears a musician playing under an awning.

verses.title: Love to the heavens
verses.heading: Faithfulness to the clouds
verses.meaning: For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds. The reason for praise is God's character. His covenant love is as high as the heavens. His faithfulness reaches to the clouds. The images are of immeasurable greatness. David's shelter under God's wings opens into a vision of love that fills the sky.
verses.context: Psalm 36:5 says, 'Your loving devotion, O LORD, reaches to the heavens,' and Ephesians 3:18 speaks of the breadth and length and height of Christ's love. Psalm 57:10 measures God's love by the sky.
explore: To the heavens
God's love is immeasurable. It reaches as high as the sky.
Faithfulness to the clouds
God's faithfulness is lofty. It rises beyond anything humans can reach or measure.
verses.reflect: How big is God's love to you? How could this verse expand your view?
verses.alt: Towering clouds rise into a deep blue sky over the wilderness.

verses.title: Your glory over all the earth
verses.heading: The refrain closes
verses.meaning: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth. The refrain from verse 5 returns to close the psalm. After danger and praise, the final word is God's glory. The repetition frames the psalm. David began in a cave hiding from Saul and ends praying for God's glory over the whole earth. The perspective has grown from personal survival to universal worship.
verses.context: Psalm 57:5 and Psalm 108:5 share these words. Numbers 14:21 says, 'As surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD.' The psalm ends where its first half ended.
explore: Repeated refrain
The words frame the psalm. They show where David's heart rests.
All the earth
God's glory covers everything. David's vision is universal.
verses.reflect: How has your perspective grown in a hard season? Could it grow toward God's glory?
verses.alt: Light pours from the cave mouth over the valley at full morning.
